articles.title: IsDB And IFAD Aim To Mobilize $750 Million For Food Systems And Rural Transformation
articles.snippet:
The Islamic Development Bank and the International Fund for Agricultural Development have signed a new Cooperation and Co-financing Agreement aimed at mobilizing up to $750 million for sustainable agricultural development, food systems, and rural transformation.
The post IsDB And IFAD Aim To Mobilize $750 Million For Food Systems And Rural Transformation appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
IsDB And IFAD Aim To Mobilize $750 Million For Food Systems And Rural Transformation
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 14, 2026
IsDB And IFAD Aim To Mobilize $750 Million For Food Systems And Rural Transformation
The Islamic Development Bank and the International Fund for Agricultural Development have signed a new Cooperation and Co-financing Agreement aimed at mobilizing up to $750 million for sustainable agricultural development, food systems, and rural transformation.
The expanded partnership will combine the institutions’ financing capabilities, development expertise, and international reach to support investments designed to strengthen food security, reduce poverty, and create economic opportunities in rural communities across their common member countries.
IsDB and IFAD are developing a joint action plan that will translate the agreement into individual investments. Priority areas include agribusiness value chains, market access, rural finance and financial inclusion, climate adaptation, sustainable natural resource management, and water access.
The agreement is also expected to expand opportunities for private-sector investment supporting agribusinesses and rural small and medium-sized enterprises. The organizations plan to combine different forms of development and commercial financing to support projects across the food and agricultural economy.
The wider IsDB Group will participate through affiliates including the Islamic Corporation for the Development of the Private Sector, the International Islamic Trade Finance Corporation, and the Islamic Corporation for the Insurance of Investment and Export Credit. The approach is intended to combine development finance, trade finance, investment, and risk mitigation capabilities.
The new agreement expands a relationship between IsDB and IFAD that dates back to 1980. Since then, the organizations have jointly financed 29 projects with a combined value of approximately $1.45 billion.
The additional $750 million mobilization target represents a significant expansion of that collaboration and is intended to increase the scale of investments addressing agricultural productivity, rural livelihoods, market connectivity, and resilience.
KEY QUOTES:
“This renewed partnership between IsDB and IFAD builds on nearly five decades of successful cooperation. Together, we will leverage our collective expertise and resources to strengthen resilience, expand opportunities, and improve the lives of rural communities across our member countries.”
Dr. Muhammad Al Jasser, Chairman Of The IsDB Group
“Through this agreement, we are scaling up investment in the first mile of food systems to create jobs, increase incomes and build more prosperous and resilient rural economies. When rural people have the opportunity to build businesses, connect to markets, and earn a decent living, the benefits extend far beyond rural areas.”
Alvaro Lario, President Of IFAD

articles.text:
DCC Energy Sells Nexora To One Equity Partners For $725 Million
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 12, 2026
DCC Energy Sells Nexora To One Equity Partners For $725 Million
DCC Energy agreed to sell its technology division, Nexora, to investment subsidiaries of funds managed or advised by One Equity Partners for an enterprise value of $725 million, cash-free and debt-free. The transaction is subject to customary regulatory approvals and is expected to close on or after March 1, 2027.
Nexora operates a group of specialist technology businesses connecting technology brands with customers across workplaces, classrooms, live entertainment, digital infrastructure, and the home.
The company said One Equity Partners will become its new owner and investment partner, providing a platform to accelerate growth and invest further in its people and capabilities.
Nexora also expects the partnership to create additional opportunities for its customers, vendor partners, and employees.
The divestiture comes as DCC Energy moves toward its previously announced acquisition by Dragon Bidco, a company indirectly owned by funds and investment vehicles advised by Energy Capital Partners and KKR.
DCC Energy and Dragon Bidco announced that acquisition on July 27, 2026, and DCC Energy shareholders approved the transaction scheme on September 18.
Under the acquisition terms, DCC Energy shareholders are entitled to receive 6,525 pence in cash per share plus potential additional consideration of as much as 125 pence per share if specified conditions related to the Nexora disposal are satisfied or waived before July 31, 2027.
Based on an assumed March 1, 2027 completion date and no specified leakage before closing, DCC Energy currently expects the Nexora transaction to generate approximately $701 million in net proceeds.
That would result in estimated additional consideration of 42 pence per DCC Energy share. The final amount will be determined after the Nexora sale closes.
If the applicable disposal conditions are not satisfied or waived by July 31, 2027, no additional consideration related to the Nexora sale would be payable to DCC Energy shareholders.
DCC Energy said Nexora has developed a strong market position during its time within the group and credited the company’s employees with contributing to its growth.
Nexora CEO Clive Fitzharris is leading the business into its next phase under One Equity Partners.
One Equity Partners is a middle-market private equity firm focused on the industrial, healthcare, and technology sectors across North America and Europe.

Jefferies International is serving as sole financial advisor to DCC Energy on the Nexora divestiture, while Hogan Lovells is acting as English legal advisor.

articles.title: Leslie’s Files Chapter 11 To Cut Debt By About $685 Million And Secure $150 Million In New Capital
articles.snippet:
Leslie's has entered into a restructuring support agreement with a group representing more than 80% of its existing lenders and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection as the pool and spa retailer seeks to substantially reduce its debt and strengthen its financial position.
The post Leslie’s Files Chapter 11 To Cut Debt By About $685 Million And Secure $150 Million In New Capital appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Leslie’s Files Chapter 11 To Cut Debt By About $685 Million And Secure $150 Million In New Capital
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 3, 2026
Leslie’s Files Chapter 11 To Cut Debt By About $685 Million And Secure $150 Million In New Capital
Leslie’s has entered into a restructuring support agreement with a group representing more than 80% of its existing lenders and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection as the pool and spa retailer seeks to substantially reduce its debt and strengthen its financial position.
The restructuring is expected to eliminate approximately $685 million, or 90%, of Leslie’s outstanding funded debt.
The agreement also includes commitments for $150 million of new capital, consisting of $90 million of new-money debtor-in-possession financing and $60 million of equity financing. Certain parties to the restructuring agreement fully backstop the equity investment.
Leslie’s has filed voluntary petitions for prearranged Chapter 11 proceedings in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Texas.
The company expects to emerge from Chapter 11 in early 2027 and anticipates that a group of its existing lenders will hold majority ownership following the restructuring.
Leslie’s said the transaction is intended to provide a deleveraged balance sheet, additional liquidity and greater financial flexibility to reinvest in its operations and customer experience.
The company is also reducing its physical retail footprint. Leslie’s announced the closure of 76 stores and said all remaining locations outside of stores that were recently closed will remain open and operational.
The retailer plans to continue evaluating its real estate portfolio during the Chapter 11 process to better align its store network with customer demand and its long-term business strategy.
Leslie’s said stores and digital operations will continue serving customers throughout the restructuring. The company is seeking court authorization to continue paying employee wages and benefits, maintain customer programs and honor vendor obligations.
Gift cards and loyalty program benefits will continue to be honored.
In addition to the $90 million new-money DIP facility, Leslie’s is seeking approval for a fully committed $225 million DIP asset-based financing facility from its existing ABL lenders.
The company said the financing arrangements are expected to provide sufficient liquidity to operate through the Chapter 11 process.
Support: Simpson Thacher & Bartlett and Haynes and Boone are serving as legal advisers. BRG is serving as financial and restructuring adviser, Centerview Partners is serving as investment banker and C Street Advisory Group is serving as strategic communications adviser. Hilco Global has been retained to assist Leslie’s with its real estate portfolio.
KEY QUOTES:
“Today’s announcement marks an important milestone in our commitment to our customers and our business. With a stronger balance sheet and greater financial flexibility, Leslie’s can reinvest across the business to strengthen operating execution and deliver an even better experience for our customers, both in-store and online. Leslie’s is here to stay, and I am deeply grateful to our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support as we work to position Leslie’s for a strong future.”
Jason McDonell, Chief Executive Officer of Leslie’s

articles.title: Accelevation Secures $650 Million Credit Agreement Led By Bank Of America, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, KeyBank And PNC
articles.snippet:
Accelevation Holdings entered into a new $650 million senior secured credit agreement that replaces credit facilities established before the company’s initial public offering and provides additional financial flexibility to support its long-term growth strategy.
The post Accelevation Secures $650 Million Credit Agreement Led By Bank Of America, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, KeyBank And PNC appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Accelevation Secures $650 Million Credit Agreement Led By Bank Of America, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, KeyBank And PNC
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 14, 2026
Accelevation Secures $650 Million Credit Agreement Led By Bank Of America, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, KeyBank And PNC
Accelevation Holdings entered into a new $650 million senior secured credit agreement that replaces credit facilities established before the company’s initial public offering and provides additional financial flexibility to support its long-term growth strategy.
The financing consists of a $400 million revolving credit facility and a $250 million Term Loan A, both of which mature in 2031. The facilities are currently priced at Term SOFR plus 1.50% to 2.50%, representing a substantial reduction from the company’s previous borrowing rate of SOFR plus 4.50% to 5.25%.
Accelevation said the new financing strengthens its balance sheet, extends its maturity profile, lowers borrowing costs, and gives the company additional flexibility to invest in its operations and pursue strategic priorities. The refinancing follows Accelevation’s transition to the public equity markets and comes as the company operates with a lower level of debt.
Bank of America served as administrative agent and collateral agent. BofA Securities, JPMorgan Chase Bank, Morgan Stanley Senior Funding, KeyBank National Association, and PNC Capital Markets served as joint lead arrangers. BofA Securities and JPMorgan Chase Bank also served as joint bookrunners.
Accelevation designs, manufactures, and installs customized structural, electrical, and mechanical systems for mission-critical infrastructure, combining U.S.-based manufacturing with nationwide field service capabilities.
KEY QUOTES:
“We are pleased to announce the closing of these new facilities, which strengthen our balance sheet and enhance our financial flexibility as we continue to execute our growth strategy. As we transition to the public equity market with a lower level of debt, it was important to access more cost-efficient capital. The new facilities extend our maturity profile, reduce our borrowing costs, and provide flexibility to continue investing in our business. We believe this capital structure positions us well to support our customers and execute our long-term strategic priorities.”
Ken Krause, Chief Financial Officer of Accelevation

articles.title: Pagaya Closes $650 Million Auto ABS Deal, Marking 100th Securitization
articles.snippet:
Pagaya Technologies closed RPM 2026-5, a $650 million asset-backed securitization backed by auto loans, marking the company’s 100th ABS transaction since completing its first securitization in 2018.
The post Pagaya Closes $650 Million Auto ABS Deal, Marking 100th Securitization appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Pagaya Closes $650 Million Auto ABS Deal, Marking 100th Securitization
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 12, 2026
Pagaya Closes $650 Million Auto ABS Deal, Marking 100th Securitization
Pagaya Technologies closed RPM 2026-5, a $650 million asset-backed securitization backed by auto loans, marking the company’s 100th ABS transaction since completing its first securitization in 2018.
The milestone brings Pagaya’s lifetime ABS issuance to more than $44 billion across multiple consumer asset classes.
Since 2018, Pagaya has raised more than $44 billion to support loan originations across personal loans, auto loans, and point-of-sale loans.
The company said it remains the primary ABS issuer of consumer unsecured loans in the U.S., supported by a diversified institutional investor base and continued demand for its securitizations.
RPM 2026-5 attracted 35 unique investors.
Five of those investors were new to Pagaya’s RPM shelf, further expanding the company’s capital markets investor base.
The transaction also brings Pagaya’s total issuance for 2026 to more than $10 billion.
Pagaya has built its securitization program around a broader capital markets platform that combines long-term committed capital with diversified funding sources.
The company said this capital structure is designed to help it scale alongside lending partners while providing institutional investors with access to AI-underwritten consumer credit assets.
Pagaya uses machine learning, a large data network, and AI-driven underwriting technologies to support consumer credit products for financial institutions, their customers, and investors.
Its proprietary API and capital solutions are integrated into partner platforms to support loan decisioning and access to financial products.
The company’s 100th securitization represents another milestone in the expansion of its capital markets business since launching its ABS program eight years ago.
KEY QUOTES:
“Closing our 100th ABS transaction is a testament to the trust our institutional partners place in Pagaya’s platform. Over the last eight years, we have intentionally built a robust capital engine powered by long-term committed capital and diversified funding sources. This foundation allows us to scale with our lending partners while continuing to offer premier investors access to high-performing, AI-underwritten consumer assets.”
Gal Krubiner, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Pagaya

articles.title: Silver Point Leads $650 Million Financing For Stryten Energy’s C&D Trojan Acquisition
articles.snippet:
Silver Point Capital's Direct Lending business has led a $650 million term loan financing supporting Stryten Energy's acquisition of C&D Technologies and Trojan Battery Company.
The post Silver Point Leads $650 Million Financing For Stryten Energy’s C&D Trojan Acquisition appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Silver Point Leads $650 Million Financing For Stryten Energy’s C&D Trojan Acquisition
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 7, 2026
Silver Point Leads $650 Million Financing For Stryten Energy’s C&D Trojan Acquisition
Silver Point Capital’s Direct Lending business has led a $650 million term loan financing supporting Stryten Energy’s acquisition of C&D Technologies and Trojan Battery Company.
Silver Point also led syndication of the financing to existing and new lenders.
Stryten completed the C&D Trojan acquisition on October 1, 2026.
The transaction creates a larger battery manufacturing platform serving transportation, industrial, essential power, critical infrastructure and military applications.
Following the acquisition, the combined company operates 18 battery manufacturing and component facilities across the United States, Mexico and China.
Stryten is a portfolio company of Atlas Holdings, while C&D Trojan was previously a portfolio company of KPS Capital Partners.
The financing extends Silver Point’s existing relationship with Stryten. The investment firm previously led a $400 million financing for the company in 2024.
KEY QUOTES:
“Silver Point is pleased to continue our partnership with Stryten and Atlas Holdings by leading this financing. This combination creates one of North America’s most comprehensive battery manufacturing and energy storage portfolios, and we are proud to provide a customized solution that supports the combined company’s next chapter of growth and enhances its ability to serve customers across critical markets.”
Anthony DiNello, Head of Direct Lending at Silver Point Capital

articles.text:
Dwight Capital And Dwight Investment Management Close $607 Million In Seniors Housing Financings During Q3 2026
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
Dwight Capital And Dwight Investment Management Close $607 Million In Seniors Housing Financings During Q3 2026
Dwight Capital and its affiliate, Dwight Investment Management, completed $607 million in seniors housing financings during the third quarter of 2026, supporting skilled nursing facilities, assisted living communities, and other healthcare real estate assets across 17 states. The transactions included HUD-insured loans, bridge financings, and revolving lines of credit (RLOCs), reflecting the firms’ continued activity in the seniors housing and healthcare financing markets.
Among the largest transactions was a $71.25 million bridge loan supporting a four-property, 646-bed skilled nursing portfolio spanning Montana and Colorado. The financing was used to acquire two facilities in the Denver metropolitan area and complete cash-out refinancings of two existing properties in Montana.
The loan features a 30-month term, a six-month extension option, and provisions for future funding. The borrower intends to increase occupancy and implement operational improvements at the newly acquired Colorado facilities before pursuing permanent financing for the portfolio. Josh Levin originated the transaction.
Another major financing involved $52 million in HUD Section 232/223(f) loans for a five-property, 577-bed skilled nursing portfolio in Arkansas. The loans will refinance existing debt, including acquisition financing associated with the sponsor’s December 2025 purchase of the facilities.
The Arkansas financing features a 35-year, fully amortizing structure, providing the borrower with long-term financing for the portfolio. Adam Offman and Yossi Benish originated the loans.
Dwight also completed several significant bridge financing transactions involving skilled nursing properties in Ohio. These included a $54.5 million bridge refinancing for a 583-bed skilled nursing portfolio, accompanied by a $9 million revolving line of credit.
Another Ohio transaction involved a $46.5 million bridge acquisition loan for a 290-bed skilled nursing facility, together with an $8.5 million revolving line of credit.
Additional transactions included a $25 million bridge refinancing for a 234-bed skilled nursing facility in Bedford, Ohio, and a $17 million bridge refinancing for a 130-bed facility in Cleveland, accompanied by a $2.5 million revolving line of credit.
Beyond skilled nursing facilities, Dwight provided an $11.4 million bridge acquisition loan for a 351-bed assisted living portfolio located in Ohio and Minnesota.
The firms also maintained substantial activity in the HUD-insured lending market during the quarter. Notable transactions included $47.2 million across four HUD Section 232/223(f) loans for a four-property, 379-bed skilled nursing portfolio in Illinois.
Additional HUD-insured financings included a $26.9 million loan for a 170-bed skilled nursing facility in New Jersey, a $26.3 million loan for a 156-bed facility in New Hampshire, and a $23.3 million loan for a 280-bed skilled nursing facility in New York.
Dwight also completed an $18.4 million HUD Section 232/223(f) loan for a 151-bed skilled nursing facility in the southeastern United States.

Since Launching in 2021, Angle Health has Emerged as the Leading Alternative to Traditional Health Insurance Plans for Small Businesses Nationwide, Now Serving More than 5,000 Employers, Offering Customized Health Plans in 47 States, and Delivering Four Consecutive Quarters of Profitability
Angle Health , the first AI-native healthcare benefits platform, today announced a $600 million equity financing at a $2.7 billion valuation, consisting of a $200 million Series C financing and a $400 million tender offer. The round, led by Vitruvian Partners with participation from new investor Town Hall Ventures and existing investors Blumberg Capital, Portage Ventures, PruVen Capital, and Y Combinator, is expected to close later this month.
The announcement comes at a time when employers are facing the largest increase in health insurance costs in two decades . Small and midsize businesses are hit especially hard, with limited options that are costly, confusing, and difficult for employees to navigate, or simply unaffordable. This dynamic impacts a growing number of Americans as the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics has consistently reported small business employment growth outpacing that of larger businesses, a trend that is poised to accelerate as AI breaks down barriers to entrepreneurship.
“Access to great healthcare shouldn’t depend on the size of the company you work for,” said Ty Wang, Co-Founder and CEO at Angle Health. “Small businesses employ tens of millions of Americans, yet they have historically had the least options available to them for healthcare coverage and almost no control over its costs. We built Angle Health to fix that. This financing enables us to reach more of the local businesses that power our country and continue to deliver a personalized, higher-quality, more affordable healthcare experience to everyday Americans. We are particularly excited to partner with Vitruvian, as we specifically sought out a group with deep expertise at the intersection of healthcare, technology, and financial services and a proven track record of successfully scaling companies through growth-oriented partnerships.”
By combining a modern, AI-driven technology platform with an integrated approach to local, personalized healthcare access, Angle Health enables employers with as few as two employees to offer their employees sophisticated, customized benefits and personalized healthcare journeys, improving experiences and outcomes across the ecosystem. Employers choosing Angle Health benefit from increased choice, transparency, and stability. Their employees have access to an expanding suite of AI-powered navigation and targeted clinical capabilities, facilitating healthier, lower-cost, and more satisfied plan members, while concurrently removing administrative friction for the clinicians serving those members. The company’s Benefit Builder platform brings unprecedented transparency to group underwriting, allowing brokers to generate firm, underwritten quotes in minutes, customize plans in real time, and access the industry’s first-of-its-kind Health Scorecard. Today, the company serves over 5,000 employers with customizable plans available in 47 states.
